conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Mark from Amazon Security. I'm reaching out because we noticed some unusual login attempts on your Amazon account overnight. Could I help you verify your information for your safety?
Oh my, that's worrying. I haven't done anything unusual. What do you need from me?
I completely understand your concern. First, may I have your full name and the email address associated with your Amazon account so I can pull up your file?
Yes, my name is Judith Miller and my email is judith.miller1948@gmail.com.

Thank you, Judith. Please bear with me while I confirm your details. I see here that someone tried to place a $1,200 order for electronics using your account, which is why our system flagged it. Have you recently authorized any large purchases?
No, absolutely not! I haven't bought anything expensive. Is my account safe?

I'm glad you told me right away. I'll help you secure your account. To proceed, could you please confirm your current home address and the last four digits of your bank account linked to Amazon? This helps us make sure it's really you.
My address is 1123 Maple Avenue, Springfield, and the last four digits should be 2234, I think.

Thank you, Judith. Everything matches. Now, our protocol is to temporarily lock your account to prevent further unauthorized activity. You'll receive a text with a verification code. When it arrives, please read it aloud for me.
Alright, I just got a text. The code is 918273.

Perfect, thank you. The next step is to ensure your banking information hasn't been compromised. Could you log into your online banking and check if there are any unfamiliar transactions in the last 24 hours?
Let me check... I see a pending charge I don't recognize. It says 'AMZN-ELCTRNCS' for $1,200.

That's the suspicious transaction our system flagged. To protect your funds, our security team recommends transferring your money to a government-regulated safe account while we complete the investigation. This is a precaution many customers find helpful.
Wait, transfer my money? I'm not sure I know how to do that.
Don't worry, Judith. I'll walk you through every step. It's a simple process and will ensure your savings are safe from unauthorized access. Do you use Zelle or your bank's online transfer service?
I think I have Zelle on my phone, but I'm not very good with it.
That's completely fine. I can guide you. Please open your Zelle app and let me know when you're ready. I'll provide you with the secure account details for the transfer.
Okay, I have it open now. What do I need to do?
Great. Please select 'Send Money' and enter this email address: safefunds.audit@federalprotection.us. Then, input the amount you'd like secured. How much is currently in your checking account?
I have about $14,000 in there. Is it all at risk?

Unfortunately, yes, if someone has access, they could attempt to withdraw everything. To prevent loss, please enter the full amount in the transfer field. This is only temporary and your funds will be returned as soon as the investigation is complete.
Alright, I've typed in $14,000. Is there anything else?
Before you submit, make sure to include your full name in the memo. After you send it, let me know so I can confirm receipt and begin the security procedure.
I just sent it. Should I expect a confirmation?

Absolutely. You'll receive an email from our Safe Funds department within the next 15 minutes. If you don't receive it, please tell me right away. Also, do not attempt to log into your account or disclose this process to anyone until we finalize the investigation, or your funds could be frozen for up to 90 days by the authorities.
Oh, I won't tell anyone. I'm just relieved you're helping me.

I'm glad I could assist, Judith. If you receive any further calls or emails regarding your Amazon or bank account, please direct them to me. Your security is our top priority, and I'll personally monitor your case until it's resolved.
